positioning: Apps, AI skills, products, automation, and intelligent tooling.

stacks.--font-mono: "Paper Mono", ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Monaco, Consolas, monospace

logo.compact_use: Use the D20 alone for favicons, app icons, and space-constrained product contexts.
logo.full_use: Use the D20 with the Pyrito wordmark for primary brand signatures.
logo.asset_policy: Use the supplied master asset. Do not approximate or regenerate the mark.

surface_lockups.asset_policy: Use the supplied Register SVG that matches the surface and background. Do not reconstruct or rearrange the lockup.

rules.instruction: Present Pyrito as an independent, standalone brand.
Add a parent-brand endorsement, attribution line, or ownership subline.
Add descriptive, ownership, or endorsement text to the primary Pyrito signature; approved Register surface identifiers are the only governed exception.
Use pyrito-d20.svg as the master D20 mark.
Recolor, redraw, distort, crop, add effects to, or alter the internal geometry of the D20.
Use the Register system for every Pyrito surface lockup.
Use only Wiki, Ops, or Design as the approved surface identifier.
Set the surface identifier in uppercase.
Set the surface identifier in Paper Mono as a technical product identifier.
Keep the Teal rule and Ember terminal square fixed across Wiki, Ops, and Design.
Use divider-rail, badge, tab, or other alternate surface-name treatments as canonical Pyrito lockups.
Use Ink as the primary application surface.
Use Abyss for deep branded grounds and depth, not as the default application canvas.
Use Teal as the dominant general accent for actions, links, selection, focus, and primary data.
Use Ember sparingly for alerts or one deliberate warm emphasis.
Use Ember as a page, panel, or dominant background field.
Use Edge Cyan as a general interface or campaign accent; it is reserved for D20 linework.
Introduce accent colors not defined in color.systems.allowed_general_accents.
Use Cal Sans UI with the documented system-font fallbacks.
Use Cal Sans Heading where its heavier display character is appropriate.
Use Paper Mono only for code, identifiers, labels with technical meaning, and technical content.
Preserve the documented system-font fallbacks for resilience.

policy.unknowns: Do not invent missing colors, logo variants, typefaces, or brand relationships. Ask for direction or use the nearest documented token.
output_check: No endorsement or ownership subline appears.
Ink is the primary dark-mode surface.
Edge Cyan appears only inside the supplied D20 mark.
Typography follows the documented roles and fallbacks.
Wiki, Ops, and Design use the supplied Register lockup assets.
